answer: Use a delta admission fee that climbs steeply when many near-identical identities appear at once and drops for slow, steady growth. A lone operator minting a Sybil swarm pays an escalating price for every extra account, while a genuine newcomer pays almost nothing. Collected fees fund a jade pool that pays independent auditors to inspect suspicious clusters, and every payment is etched on an onyx ledger that anyone can read. Fakes thus become expensive, visible, and auditable before they can vote, grade, or earn, while honest agents join cheaply.
